requirement:
The Habeas crate MUST have a Cargo integration test that exercises evidence
authoring against a real configured Bedrock model when AWS credentials can be
loaded. It MUST skip before reading configuration or resolving credentials when
the `CI` environment variable is present. Outside CI, it MUST fail when no
Bedrock authoring configuration exists, and MUST skip with a visible warning when
the AWS SDK cannot load credentials. Skip warnings MUST be visible under ordinary
`cargo test` output.

`HABEAS_LIVE_CONFIG`, when set, MUST select a named authoring configuration for
the test. Otherwise the test MUST use the configuration that authoring would
select for the checkout under {cite}`requirements.authoring.configuration_precedence`
when it is a Bedrock configuration, falling back to the first Bedrock
configuration in name order among the user and workspace configurations. The
fixture project MUST resolve the selected name against the same workspace
authoring configurations as the checkout. Malformed configuration and invalid explicit
selections MUST fail the test. The selected profile, region, model, and options
MUST come from that configuration; credential resolution MUST use the AWS SDK.

Once credentials load, model-request and authoring failures MUST fail the test
rather than be treated as skips. The test MUST exercise an additional source read
and judgment submission using a temporary project and stdout evidence output,
without changing the checkout's evidence. It MUST retain ordinary usage history
and check the returned evidence and recorded usage. Deterministic tests MUST
verify the CI and missing-credential skip paths and the missing-configuration
failure without calling a model.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider`
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`
{cite}`requirements.authoring.submission`
{cite}`requirements.authoring.persistence`
{cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_storage`
rationale:
No gaps found. `tests/live_bedrock.rs` is auto-discovered by Cargo as an integration test: `Cargo.toml` has no `[[test]]` section or `autotests` setting that would exclude it. This requirement is itself a test requirement, so the three tests carrying `{test}` references are the deliverable. I read all three tests and their helpers, but not the production code they drive.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**
- **Live test against a real model.** `tests/live_bedrock.rs#fn[live_bedrock_authoring]` builds a temporary fixture project and runs `author-evidence` against the selected Bedrock configuration with `--stdout`. It asserts success, the `requirement` text, a valid `determination`, and a nonempty `rationale`. It requires an input for `src/parity.rs` with a selector and hash but no text, which proves the extra source read. It asserts `!project.join("evidence").exists()`. It reads the usage record and checks `backend`, `model`, `outcome == completed`, `evidence_output == stdout`, `evidence_written == true`, `request_count >= 2`, and `tool_calls.submit_judgment == 1`. It also requires at least one `habeas` or `ripgrep` call. Because it never overrides the state root, the ordinary usage history is retained.
- **Skip before reading configuration when `CI` is present.** The first statement of `live_bedrock_authoring` checks `CI` and returns after a warning.
  - `fn[live_test_prerequisites_are_checked_without_inference]` verifies it. It writes a malformed user config, runs the probe with `CI=true`, and asserts success plus the skip warning. That shows the config was never read.
- **Fail outside CI when no Bedrock configuration exists.** `.expect("no Bedrock authoring configuration…")` fails the test.
  - The probe test covers three cases: no config file, an empty config, and an Ollama-only config. It asserts a failure that is not a skip.
- **Skip with a visible warning when the SDK cannot load credentials.** `fn[credentials_available]` uses the AWS SDK loader with the configured profile and region, and `report` prints the warning.
  - The probe test uses an empty credentials file and asserts success, the "AWS credentials unavailable" warning, and no `Usage:` line.
- **Warnings visible under ordinary `cargo test`.** `fn[report]` writes directly to stderr. `fn[skip_probe]` runs the test binary without `--nocapture`, and the probe test asserts the warning appears in that stderr.
- **`HABEAS_LIVE_CONFIG`, precedence, and fallback.** `fn[selected_config]` reads the variable and `fn[select_config]` implements the selection:
  - An explicit name must resolve and be Bedrock.
  - Otherwise it applies project selection, then workspace default, then user default, and only if that choice is Bedrock.
  - Otherwise it falls back to the first Bedrock configuration in name order across user and workspace names.
  - `fn[live_configuration_selection_follows_authoring_precedence]` covers each branch. That includes skipping an earlier Ollama config and falling back from an Ollama default. It also covers the explicit override.
  - The same test shows profile, region, model, and options coming from the selected record.
- **Fixture resolves against the checkout's workspace authoring configurations.** `select_config` returns a `habeas.toml` text trimmed to `version` and `authoring`. The selection test asserts the `gamma` config is present and `evidence` is absent. `live_bedrock_authoring` writes that file and passes `--config <name>`.
- **Malformed configuration and invalid explicit selections fail.** The selection test covers an explicit Ollama name, an unknown name, a malformed user config, and a malformed workspace config. The probe test covers a malformed user config and an unknown explicit name through `HABEAS_LIVE_CONFIG`.
- **Model-request and authoring failures fail once credentials load.** The probe test supplies fake static credentials and an unreachable endpoint. It asserts a non-success exit, the "live Bedrock authoring failed" message, and no skip warning.
- **Deterministic tests for the CI and missing-credential skips and for the missing-configuration failure.** The probe test above runs all three without calling a model.

The cited requirements (`provider`, `source_tools`, `submission`, `persistence`, `usage_storage`) are context. The live test exercises them end to end, and the selection logic follows `configuration_precedence`.

:::{req} configuration_precedence
`--config <name>` MUST select a configuration for that invocation. Otherwise,
authoring MUST use the user's selection for the canonical project root, then the
workspace default, then the user's default. Named workspace configurations MUST
override same-named user configurations as complete records. Backend, model,
connection settings, and options MUST come from the selected record as a unit;
fields MUST NOT be merged between records. Workspace-only authoring MUST work
without a user configuration file. Missing configuration or an unknown selection
MUST identify the relevant configuration file and point to documented examples.
An explicit Bedrock AWS profile or region MUST override the corresponding SDK
default; omitted values MUST use standard AWS SDK resolution. Ollama MUST use
its configured endpoint or `http://localhost:11434`. If `api_key_env` is set, its
named variable MUST supply the credential; a missing or empty value MUST produce
an error before a model request.
:::{req} provider
The authoring harness MUST use Rig and support Bedrock and Ollama. Users MUST be
able to select a backend and model through configuration without changing the
assessment tools, prompt, or evidence format.
:::{req} source_tools
The harness MUST expose a `habeas` tool accepting exactly one of these request
forms. Each form MUST correspond to one existing evidence-input kind:
| Request fields | Evidence input returned | Definition |
| `file: String`, `line_start: Integer`, optional `line_end: Integer` | Outline inputs for the innermost outline nodes covering the range | {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` |
| `file: String`, `item: String` | Outline input | {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` |
| `requirements: String` | Requirements input, including its matching names | {cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs` |
| `definition: String` | Definition input | {cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs` |
Selector arguments MUST use the syntax defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Reads MUST use the current
project working tree, including unstaged changes to tracked files and staged new
files. By default, source inputs MUST stay within the project root after
resolving symlinks; in a Git worktree, both the requested file and its resolved
target MUST be present in the Git index. Projects outside Git MUST use the same
containment rules without requiring an index. Failure to read an existing
repository's index MUST be reported as an error.
The project-root `evidence/` directory MUST be excluded from model reads by
default, including symlink aliases. Every source the harness supplies to the
model MUST be redacted under {cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. Generated build outputs MUST follow
{cite}`requirements.authoring.generated_inputs`. Workspace path overrides MUST
follow {cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`, including explicit
permission for otherwise excluded inputs. A denied mandatory input MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`, and a denied model
read MUST return a tool error under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
Line numbers are only a way to request sources; recorded evidence MUST identify
sources by outline selector and structural hash, never by line number. Request
line numbers MUST be one-based and inclusive, and omitting `line_end` MUST read
through EOF. A line-range request MUST be resolved to the innermost outline
nodes covering the requested lines, which are `line` nodes in a file using the
plain-text profile; the result MUST show the model each node's selector and
source text, without line numbers, and the harness MUST record those nodes as
outline inputs. The model-facing tool description MUST include the argument conventions
from the cited requirements, including outline selector syntax, definition
selections, and full definition names, with a short request example for each form.
A successful call MUST return the requested evidence input, populated by the
harness with the selected source text, using the existing evidence schema.
{cite}`requirements.ci.schema`
Required terminology dependencies MUST be returned alongside it as additional
definition inputs under {cite}`requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs`.
The result MUST have this shape:
```text
HabeasResult {
input: EvidenceInput,
definitions: Array<DefinitionInput>,
`definitions` MUST be empty when no additional terminology is required. The
harness MUST record inputs supplied to the model in the assessment's evidence.
A failed read MUST add no evidence input. Access-policy denials MUST be handled
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`; other failed reads MUST return
an explanatory tool error.
:::{req} submission
The harness MUST expose a `submit_judgment` tool accepting exactly these fields:
```text
submit_judgment({ determination: Judgment, rationale: String })
Judgment = Boolean | { FIXME: Array<String> }
The judgment MUST use the three outcomes and nonempty FIXME entries defined by
{cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`.
`rationale` MUST be nonempty Markdown. This tool call MUST supply the final
assessment result. The model MUST invoke it exactly once over the entire
assessment. If a response ends without invoking it, and the assessment has
not already been reminded, the harness MUST continue the conversation with one
user message, `Reminder: you MUST submit your result with the submit_judgment
tool.`, naming the assessment's submission tool. If a later response also ends
without invoking it, or the model invokes it more than once, the harness MUST
report an error and leave existing evidence unchanged. The reminder MUST be
counted in usage like any other turn.
The harness MUST check the complete model response for multiple submissions
before accepting one. Invalid submission arguments MUST also fail the assessment.
A valid single submission MUST finish the assessment; there is no submission
repair or resubmission loop, except the one continuation after a response cut
off at its output limit under {cite}`requirements.authoring.output_limit`, the
one reminder above, and the one resubmission after a rejection under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.rejection`. An assessment that fails before accepting a valid
judgment MUST emit no evidence JSON to stdout.
:::{req} persistence
After one valid judgment, the harness MUST write the subject text, submitted
determination and rationale, and recorded inputs using the existing evidence
schema. {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`
By default, it MUST write the subject's evidence file. With `--stdout`, it MUST
emit a single evidence JSON object followed by a newline to stdout and MUST NOT
create or change evidence files or directories. All three outcomes MUST be
written to the selected destination as completed assessments; their validation
status MUST follow {cite}`requirements.ci.determination`.
:::{req} usage_storage
Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`.
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
Failed, cancelled, or unfinished
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
